Subject: Cross-zone switchover qualification for Helmia Health

Hi Laura / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick post-call recap and action items so we have alignment from both sides. I captured the bits that matter for residency/failover and data handling.

Key asks from Helmia on the call:
- Primary requirement: keep PHI/PII resident in US region by default; some EU patient data may require replication to EU warm-standby.
- Failover model: cross-zone switchover within country for AZ-level incidents; cross-region warm-standby only for specific EU-subset.
- Recovery objectives: target RTO = 15 minutes (critical paths), RPO = 1 hour for model state and customer artifacts.
- Logs & audit: immutable audit logs for 365 days; ability to redact or mask PII in application logs before retention.
- Keys: customer-managed KMS for Private deployment; clarification needed for Dedicated/Hosted.
- Backups: encrypted snapshots of KV cache / application state; requirement for at-rest encryption using a customer key for EU backups.

Attachments: I attached the Helmia data-handling questionnaire you started (Helmia-Data-Handling-Questionnaire.pdf).

Open questions for you (please confirm):
1) Do you need the EU warm-standby to be a live hot replica (sync) or a warm standby with periodic snapshot replication?
2) Is per-tenant keying required for EU-resident patients, or will an org-level customer-managed key be sufficient?
3) Any specific compliance artifact we should include up front (SOC2 coverage specific controls, FedRAMP if relevant)?

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Ben (cc) will provide technical detail on how Redwood handles KV cache replication, snapshot cadence, and log retention options.
- We’ll share a simple region-failover diagram and a short runbook for the switchover scenarios (attachment forthcoming).
- Schedule a 30-minute technical deep dive with your infra/security team (Ben + Aditya + me).

If you confirm the EU warm-standby model preference (hot vs warm snapshot), we’ll draft a recommended runbook and an estimated cost delta for maintaining the warm standby.

Thanks —

Thanks, Irene — that recap is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- For EU patients (we have a small clinical research cohort), we prefer a warm standby in EU (periodic snapshots, not a full live sync) — cost sensitivity is high for that subset.
- Per-tenant keying: we would like per-tenant (per-organization) keys for EU-resident datasets if available, otherwise one customer-managed key per Helmia org.
- Logs: we need the ability to redact patient identifiers before logs are forwarded to long-term storage; also need proof that audit logs are tamper-evident.

Two quick asks before the deep dive: can your team confirm whether the KV cache is included in backups by default and whether snapshots are encrypted with the same KMS key used for object storage? Also, please flag any compliance artifacts you can provide for our security review.

If you can send the failover diagram and runbook draft, I’ll loop in our security team (security@helmiahealth.com) so they can spot-check.

Best,
Laura
Director, Infrastructure & Security
Helmia Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Cross-zone switchover qualification for Helmia Health — technical notes

Irene / Aditya — notes to answer Laura’s questions and give a runbook baseline. Pasted below so we can incorporate in the customer-facing doc.

1) KV cache and snapshots
- By default KV cache is in-memory and not replicated cross-region. For stateful recovery we recommend periodic encrypted snapshots exported to customer-owned object storage (S3/GCS) or Redwood-managed encrypted blob store.
- Snapshot cadence is configurable; typical pattern: 1h snapshots for critical tenants (meets RPO=1h). Snapshots include pointer metadata, not raw unredacted PII unless the app stores PII in the cache (call that out).
- Snapshots are encrypted at rest. For Hosted/Dedicated we can use Redwood-managed keys; for Private we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS). For EU warm-standby, snapshots destined for EU storage can be encrypted with the customer-specified EU KMS key.

2) Warm standby vs hot replica
- Warm standby (snapshot-based) is supported and is the lower-cost option. It requires an automated restore step in the warm region; typical switchover prep: pre-provisioned compute in EU kept in hot-warm state so restore for critical paths can be initiated within the 15m RTO for minimal service surface (we’ll need to size accordingly).
- Hot live sync across regions is possible but requires continuous cross-region replication (higher cost and network egress). Not recommended unless you need zero-RPO.

3) Logs, redaction, and audit
- We offer log pipelines with transform hooks. You can redact fields upstream (recommended) or use Redwood’s transform layer. We’ll provide sample configs for common PII fields.
- Audit logs are immutable once written and signed; we can provide a tamper-evident export and retention settings up to multi-year retention.

4) Runbook sketch (high level)
- Detection: AZ failure -> traffic routed to regional standby within AZs; if region degraded, trigger automated failover to warm-standby (restore snapshot + warm state).
- Pre-cutover checks: snapshot integrity, KMS access check, DNS TTL swap plan, health probes.
- Post-cutover: replay any queued ops, confirm audit log continuity, escalate to on-call infra owners.

I’ll prepare a short (1 page) diagram and a checklist we can share with the customer. Also include suggested snapshot cadences and estimated cost delta for warm-standby EU (ballpark).

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
